report:
Findings: No significant knee effusion. There is a horizontal tear of the body of the lateral meniscus with early para meniscal cyst formation. Normal medial meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.   The normal tibiofemoral and trochlear articular cartilage. Focal fissuring of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage is noted with underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Lateral meniscal tear with early para meniscal cyst formation. Medial patellar chondromalacia. No ligamentous injury.

A. Ligaments  
 ACL: intact  
 PCL: intact 
 MCL: Deep MCL partial tear  
 LCL complex: Increased signal intensity at the femoral side of the fibular collateral ligament. The popliteus tendon, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band are intact.  
  
 B. Menisci  
 Medial meniscus: no definite tear.  
 Lateral meniscus: suspicious for anterior root partial tear with erosion of the subjacent bone,  
  
 C. Extensor Mechanism  
 Distal quadriceps tendon: Normal.  
 Patellar tendon: Normal.  
 Patella: Normally located in the femoral groove.  
 Medial plicae and suprapatellar plicae are present.  
  
 D. Fluid  and  Soft Tissue  
 Joint effusion and fluid in suprapatellar bursa is seen. Several thin septations in the suprapatellar bursa is also present.  
 No soft tissue mass.  
 No Baker's cyst is seen. No other spaceoccupying lesion is visualized.  
  
 E. Osseous Structures  and  Articular Cartilages  
  Focal bone erosion intact9xintact5 cm at anteromedial part of  lateral tibial plateau

  Osteophyte formation of the medial compartment; OA medial compartment Lateral meniscus: suspicious for anterior root partial tear with erosion of the subjacent bone

  Low grade osteochondral injury at mid medial femoral condyle and mid lateral femoral condyle and also posterior lateral femoral condyle.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
The lateral compartment, there is suspected small radial free edge tear at the body of the lateral meniscus. There is focal osteochondral fracture at mid weight-baring lateral femoral condyle (about intact6* intact7 cm). 
The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact. 
In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. 
There is grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers).The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact. Interstitial partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon. The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The extensor mechanism is normal. 
Some amount of right knee effusion with synovitis is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. 
IMPRESSION: 
-- Focal osteochondral fracture at mid weight-baring lateral femoral condyle (about intact6* intact7 cm). 
-- Suspected small radial free edge tear at the body of the lateral meniscus. 
-- Grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers). 
-- Interstitial partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon. 
-- Some amount of right knee effusion with synovitis.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  [Age] ongoing lists knee pain with minimal imaging findings on x-ray and ultrasound. The radiologist recommend arranging MRI to further investigate.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Background of intrasubstance degeneration of the medial and lateral meniscus. 

Complex undersurface tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with the formation 2 mm the parameniscal cyst (401:109). In addition, there is a horizontal cleavage tear extending through the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus extending into the lateral meniscal body. No lateral meniscal extrusion.

Inferiorly surfacing oblique tear posterior horn of the medial meniscus with 4 mm parameniscal cyst (401:194). There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament.

PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Insertional tendinosis of the popliteus tendon.

Scattered area of high-grade chondrosis with full-thickness cartilage loss noted along the patellar surface of the patellofemoral compartment, on a background of generalized cartilage thinning. There is also generalized thinning of lateral femorotibial articular cartilage foci of full-thickness cartilage denuding involving the posterior nonweightbearing aspect lateral femoral condyle and the central weightbearing aspect lateral tibial plateau. Within the medial femorotibial compartment, is moderate chondrosis.

Trace volume joint effusion.

Scattered subcutaneous edema more pronounced along the anterior aspect the knee.

The extensor mechanism, quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered subcentimeter cysts at the popliteal fossa.

INTERPRETATION:

Complex tear posterior horn lateral meniscus with additional horizontal cleavage tear involving the body and anterior horn. Parameniscal cyst formation as described. No lateral meniscal extrusion.

Inferiorly subtle tear posterior horn medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion and parameniscal cyst formation as described.

Tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral and lateral femorotibial compartments. Findings are in keeping with moderate OA.
